kinds.d: Cumin seed from Cuminum cyminum, whole or ground.
Dried, boiled and ground rhizome of Curcuma longa, a deep orange-yellow powder with a warm, bitter flavour.
Dried fruit of Coriandrum sativum, citrusy and nutty; large-fruited types are ground for the spice trade.
Dried, scraped rhizome of ginger ground to powder; sharper than fresh and used in baking.
Seeds of white (Sinapis alba), brown (Brassica juncea) or black (Brassica nigra) mustard, fried whole or ground.
Dried fruit of Foeniculum vulgare with an anise-like flavour; green seeds are best for cooking.
Dehydrated, ground garlic or onion used in blends and seasoned salts; keep dry to avoid clumping.
Dried leaves sold singly or mixed: oregano, thyme, bay leaf, rosemary, basil, mint and dill.

brands.d: Maryland spice maker founded in Baltimore; owns Schwartz, Club House, Ducros, Kamis and Old Bay.

notes: No independent test winners or SKU models were retrieved, so only the old Rajah cumin model is kept; Rajah, MDH, Everest, TRS, Simply Organic, Burlap & Barrel and The Spice House are not given register entries (no retrieved sources). Everyday spices carry whole/ground as t; dried herbs are one kind with herb names as t.
